reviews.text: Loving this so far. It brings back such great memories of TradeWars and nails the feel and gameplay, all while updating it with 40 years worth of game design evolution and refinement. Can't wait to dig into this more (and without the daily turn limits, and the modem disconnecting from the BBS when someone picked up the phone)! I'll update my review as I play more, but already I can see how the deviations from the original will increase the gameplay depth and fix some of the few shortcomings of the original inspiration.
Seems pretty fun so far! Will post more as i play more
A huge potential for this indie title. Roadmap looks packed and realistic. Art direction is right down my alley. This is a worthy addition to any space game library.
Fun and well made from what I've seen so far. Been waiting for a game like this for a long while. Excited to see more of it and for features yet to come!

Of what I've played so far, pretty good. What you see in the demo, will give you a pretty good idea of how the game is. Though iirc it doesn't really show what the ship upgrades are like, but basically you have module slots, and you buy modules to put in it. A lot of them are tradeoff style though, you pick something to boost, and weaken something else a little. Like a combat ship doesn't need that much cargo space, or if you have a string of colonies with fuel stations, then being a little more fuel inefficient doesn't matter that much. And yeah, your colonies have upgrade slots too, though these are more pure upgrades, taking into account they have upkeep costs. Early game grind doesn't seem that bad. I did a few trade loops that I was fortunate to get where it's just 2 jumps either way, and I managed to get myself a Merchant Cruiser. Which seems like a good jack of all trades ship. Now it feels like I can more or less do what I want. Or at least it no longer feels like I have to scrape for everything.

Flashback to the 90s! TradeWars! I love how you can change the CRT settings to even get back to feels of playing in the 80s too! The blend of TradeWars and perhaps Eve Online makes this all the more fun. Looking forward to seeing the development of this game progress. The game play of bouncing around from warp to warp, selling commodities and bumping into the enemy. I can't wait for more updates. Such a cool idea and concept here.
Very Deep and addictive but without a crushing learning curve a breath of fresh air in the early access game space. The dev is patient and receptive and has curated a well built game. GG
Impressed so far after completing both tutorials. I'm excited to see what the main game has to offer. Roadmap looks very promising as well
A promising start. I'll update this when I've played more but I know it makes a difference to get a bunch of reviews

Low key excellent game. Hits you in the nostalgia for sure, but its more than that. Theres a complexity and depth that isn't fully shown off in the demo. You can colonise planets and set them up as fuel bases, as manufacturing hubs, credit farms, all sort of things. Ship have a bunch of modular customisation. Theres a bit to learn on the economy side, trading between factions and frontier systems. Theres just a lot for an early access game at this price point and I know the Dev has a heap planned between EA and 1.0. Theres also a really nice sense of a simulation happening around you, things happening and changing. A bit like the dwarf fortress world simulation. Worth the buy to support something unique and special in my opinion. If in doubt try the demo, its free. Running this on linux, does require some tinkering to get working, but the steam forum has a write up on what to do. Dev is aware and has it on their to-do list to add linux support.

Would you like to play a game? Man, this one really hits the nostalgia vibes. Dont be thrown by the bitmaps and wireframes, theres a lot going on under the hood. When I started to play I had lots of ideas of how the game could expand and through the course of playing I found them - ship customization, a dynamic world, and a ton more. Loving it so far, 10/10 no notes
Excellent game. Solid concept and execution. Looking forward to further development.
It has potential

Crisp & minimalist UI, enjoying the ability to use text commands. Would benefit from a 'Do you want to load/save' popup, and autocomplete/ more shortcuts. Looking forward to seeing how colonies/fleets get expanded on.
Very well made immersive game. The story telling and detail. Chef's kiss.

Warp to Sector One immediately passes the vibe check, with stellar (heh) visual and audio design. The game is also chock-full of tastefully obfuscated mechanics and events to discover - never frustrating instead delightful to stumble upon. Really looking forward to seeing how the game grows during its EA period. Already a solid buy for anyone who enjoys space-themed exploration/discovery-heavy experiences!

In Warp to Sector One, the main gameplay loop involves warping to new sectors to explore them, finding ports and checking their prices on Ore, Organics, and Equipment, identifying profitable trade routes, and then flying back and forth buying and selling for as long as it remains possible and profitable to do so. If you run into pirates, you can fight them in turn-based battles where you choose a stance (Aggressive, Balanced, Defensive, or Evasive), manage heat, and can optionally use fighters in a number of formations or perform utility actions like repairing or targeting the enemy's weapons or engines. There's a sort of paper-rock-scissors aspect to it, but there's also a notification at the top of the screen saying basically, "Enemy will play rock - play paper", so I've never lost a fight against pirates. You can hire captains to escort you, guard locations, or trade automatically, and colonize planets by sending down colonists and paying a startup fee, and they'll produce Ore, Organics, or Equipment for you automatically. The game also includes diplomacy, missions, buying new ships and upgrading the current one. Overall, I feel like the game does everything ok, but it doesn't really present any challenge, and very little depth to any of its mechanics. Making money while trading is trivially easy - with only three resources you can often find adjacent ports that will each buy what the other is selling and just ping-pong between them until they're out. In combat, you just do what the indicator tells you to do, and although you could do something else, you don't really have enough information to know the effect of each option. It's not a bad game, and I have no doubt it will become better, but after a couple of hours, I feel like you've seen all there is to see.

game is good but is missing some basic conquering gameplay : - expansion- you can colonise some planets but your empire does not expand , you can raid enemy faction colonies but you are not able to wipe them to 0 to make them neutral and available to you to colonize and expand your borders . NPC factions expand but you cant and this is some big minus that I hope will be resolved asap. Overall game is good and i will back to it when more update is done.

I'm writing this during the first week of Early Access, so my opinion will almost certainly evolve as the game grows. The game already has a solid foundation for a sandbox experience. If you're familiar with TradeWars 2002, you'll feel right at home, even though this is currently a single-player experience. Right now it's still fairly barebones, which is completely understandable for an Early Access title. What stands out is the potential. Once the developer continue adding features, refining the balance, and expanding the gameplay systems, I can easily see this becoming a deep, rewarding, and incredibly fun empire-building sandbox. I'm genuinely excited to see where the developer take this and look forward to future updates. The foundation is strong, and I think this has the makings of something really special.
小品级游戏，内容不多，也就2-3小时。价格有点高了，10块钱差不多。
Takes me back to my TW2002 days. I missed everything about those days except for the screech of the 2400 baud modem. Now, with this game, I can play without that screech. Thanks.

\O/ wow..... This game is ALL meat. Instead of insulting you with vapid shallow visuals, the real effort was put into making the [b]game[/b] fun. Unexpected details and touches everywhere that bring what appears to be a simple game play loop to life. I thought I'd get bored jumping between stars trading, but there's so much going on, that you get distracted (specilly if ur ADD) by bounties, missions, lore, battles, faction relations, guilds, ship outfitting, colonies, and, and, and, !! Early access, but already very playable, deeper then expected and FUN.
